Summer Traditions

The trips we take every year

Some places aren’t a once-in-a-lifetime journey. They’re the ones we come back to, summer after summer.

Lake Owassa · Sussex County, New Jersey

Our little slice of heaven

Every summer, for as much time as we can steal. Lake Owassa is where the year slows down: mornings on the dock, afternoons on the water, and evenings that end with the sun going down behind Kittatinny Mountain.

275acres of water
866 ftabove sea level
Long Pondits original name

Tucked into Frankford Township on the edge of the Kittatinny Ridge, the lake is fed by runoff from the mountain and by Bear Swamp, and spills out into Culver’s Lake before joining the Paulins Kill. Its name sounds Lenape, but it isn’t: “Owassa” comes from a fictional character in a long poem written by a Branchville clergyman for his late wife.

🛶Time on the lake

Swimming, paddling, fishing off the dock and doing absolutely nothing at all. The best part of every summer.

🌲Stokes State Forest

Right next door: the trails of Tillman Ravine, and the view from Sunrise Mountain on the Appalachian Trail.

🏞️Delaware Water Gap

A short drive away: the river, waterfalls and the climb up Mount Tammany in the national recreation area.

Labor Day · Down the Shore

One last weekend of summer

Labor Day down the shore is a tradition that began when Mom was still with us, and one we’ve kept every year since. For five summers we went to Ocean City together. She passed in May 2020, and that September we carried on: a little further south, but still the last weekend of summer, by the sea, together.
